items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: The interviewee discusses composing music for the TV show 'Dan August' but does not mention a personal relationship with a person named Dan August.

ctx.x: mathematics involved. Once you decide what the right tempo is, what feels right, you can then determine what that is in terms of a metronome beat, which of course you have to translate to frames per second, a 12-frame click — well film runs at 24 frames per second. So a 24-frame click meant it went one click every second. A 12-frame click, half of that, would be a click every half a second. And then everything in between. So there was this book the Carroll Knudson book. And this guy should have gotten an award…

Regarding themes for the subsequent shows you did after “Dan August,” music sometimes can convey emotions and sometimes music is just music. So was your task to read the description of what this show’s going to be about, maybe about the characters you know, it’s a cop but he’s got marital trouble, he’s got a young kid etcetera, and how much did the music you were trying to write reflect the story?

Right. Great question. Well obviously — needless to say — music for films and television is a highly subjective matter. And so the good news for me, for me as a composer, is I get to see the film for the first time when it’s basically complete except for the music. I cannot tell you how many times I’ve said I don’t want to read the script, I don’t want to see it halfway edited, because I want to see as close as you can get to the final product as possible before you show it to me. Now that’s not always possible.…
